This section describes the tagging scheme specific to French railway signalling, based on the [[Tag:railway%3Dsignal|international railway signal]] tagging model.

== JOSM Presets ==
Dedicated [https://josm.openstreetmap.de/wiki/Presets JOSM presets] are available for download directly from the application to simplify the mapping of [[#Tagging|French railway signalling]] according to these specifications. Please see [https://noeldev.github.io/FrenchRailwaySignalling/ French railway signalling JOSM Presets] for more information.

==Tagging==

All railway signals must include the following tags:

* {{Tag|railway|signal}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:direction||({{TagValue|railway:signal:direction|forward}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:direction|backward}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:direction|both}})}} Direction of the signal relative to the direction of the way.
* {{Tag|railway:signal:position||({{TagValue|railway:signal:position|left}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:position|right}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:position|bridge}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:position|catenary_mast}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:position|ground}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:position|in_track}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:position|overhead}})}} Lateral or vertical position of the signal relative to the track.
* {{Tag|railway:position:exact||365.913}} where ''365.913'' is an example. Position of the signal along the track. This corresponds to the kilometric point (PK) of the signal installation, measured from the beginning of the line.
* {{TagKey|railway:signal:main}}''':ref'''=123456 where '''main''' is an example of one of the [https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag:railway%3Dsignal#List_of_signal_categories signal categories] and ''123456'' is an example of an '''idreseau''' identifier assigned by [https://www.sncf-reseau.com/ SNCF Réseau]. The '''idreseau''' value is unique for each physical signalling element represented by the node (signal, board, or sign).

Optional tags:
* {{Tag|ref|}}: identifier shown on the marker plate ('''plaque de repérage''') when present.

===Notes===
On this page, the <code>railcar</code> signal category covers [https://wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_multiple_unit Electric Multiple Units] (EMUs) and [https://wikipedia.org/wiki/Diesel_multiple_unit Diesel Multiple Units] (DMUs), collectively called ''automoteurs'' in French.

===Stop signals===

====Carré====

An absolute stop signal for normal train operations, typically found on main lines or at stations. The signal displays two steady red lights, arranged either vertically or horizontally. It is equipped with a clearing light (French: '''œilleton'''), which is illuminated in all states except when the signal is closed (i.e. displaying the {{TagValue|railway:signal:main:states|FR:C}} state). The signal also features an ''identification plate'' (French: '''Plaque d'Identification''') bearing the inscription '''Nf''' in white letters on a black background.

The signal may also be equipped with a ''marker plate'' (French: '''Plaque de Repérage''') and/or a ''block system identification plate'' (French: '''plaque de cantonnement''') indicating the ''block system'' beyond the signal. The inscriptions on these plates are written in black letters on a white background.

<gallery>
File:Carre_C_BAL.svg|Carré aspect on a C-type signal head.
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:main|FR:C}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:form|light}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:shape||({{TagValue|railway:signal:main:shape|FR:C}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:main:shape|FR:F}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:main:shape|FR:H}})}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:states|}} (→ [[FR:Key:railway:signal:main:states|available states]], separated by <code>;</code>)

Optional tags:

'''Features'''
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:clearing_light|no}} (if not equipped with a clearing light)

'''Block system identification plate'''
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:type||({{TagValue|railway:signal:main:type|FR:BM}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:main:type|FR:PR}})}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:caption|}} (text displayed on the plate)

=====Carré (dwarf)=====

<gallery>
File:Signal_Carre_reduit.svg|Carré aspect on a dwarf [[#Carré|Carré]] signal.
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:main|FR:C}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:form|light}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:height|dwarf}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:states||}} (→ [[FR:Key:railway:signal:main:states|available states]], separated by <code>;</code>)

Optional tags:
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:arrangement|vertical}} (''horizontal'' by default)

===== Signal de milieu de quai (2TMV) =====

<gallery>
File:Signal de milieu de quai.svg|Illuminated white cross aspect on an intermediate signal
</gallery>

Also known as an ''intermediate signal'', this is a horizontal [[#Carré_(dwarf)|dwarf Carré]] signal used on platforms to manage two trains on the same track (French: '''2 Trains sur une Même Voie'''). It features a standard dwarf layout supplemented by a central light capable of displaying an ''illuminated white cross''. This system offers high operational flexibility, allowing two railcars to enter the platform sequentially (either from the same or opposite directions) to either depart independently or couple together.

Depending on the operational scenario, the signal presents the following aspects:
* '''Carré''': Closed to stop an incoming train at the middle of the platform. This aspect is announced by the upstream signal presenting a [[Tag:railway:signal:main:states=FR:A|Caution]] (''Avertissement'') aspect combined with a flashing [[#Yellow_band|illuminated horizontal yellow band]].
* '''Illuminated White Cross''': Cancels the signal when a multiple-unit train enters and occupies the entire platform, or when an incoming single-unit is routed to stop at the end of the second half of the platform. In these cases, the upstream ''Caution'' signal is presented without the flashing ''illuminated yellow band''.
* '''Caution''': Displayed when the station's exit signal is open (e.g., displaying a [[Tag:railway:signal:main:states=FR:RR|Rappel 30]]), ensuring the train does not exceed 30 km/h between the intermediate and exit signals.
* '''Flashing Red''': Opens after an initial stop at the [[Tag:railway:signal:main:states=FR:C|Carré]] to authorize a low-speed (15 km/h max) entry and safe coupling onto a railcar already stationary at the second half of the platform.

* {{Tag|railway:signal:main|FR:C}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:form|light}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:function|intermediate}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:states||({{TagValue|railway:signal:main:states|FR:C}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:main:states|FR:(S)}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:main:states|FR:X}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:main:states|FR:A}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:main:states|FR:VL}})}}

=====Carré (mechanical)=====

<gallery>
File:CarreMecanique.svg|Mechanical [[#Carré|Carré]] signal.
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:main|FR:C}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:form|sign}}

====Carré violet====

An absolute stop signal, similar to the [[#Carré|Carré signal]], specifically used to control train movements during shunting operations, on service tracks, or at the transition between service tracks and main lines. It may be provided either as a mechanical board or as a light signal.

The light form displays a single steady purple light. Like the Carré signal, it is equipped with an identification plate bearing the inscription '''Nf''' in white letters on a black background and may also be equipped with a marker plate and/or a block plate with inscriptions in black letters on a white background.

<gallery>
File:CV_C_BAL.svg|Cv aspect on a C-type signal head.
File:CV_A_BAL.svg|Cv aspect on an A-type signal head.
File:CV_Sol.svg|Cv aspect on a K-type signal head.
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:main|FR:CV}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:form|light}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:shape||({{TagValue|railway:signal:main:shape|FR:A}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:main:shape|FR:C}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:main:shape|FR:F}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:main:shape|FR:H}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:main:shape|FR:K}})}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:states|}} (→ [[FR:Key:railway:signal:main:states|available states]], separated by <code>;</code>)

Optional tags:

* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:type||({{TagValue|railway:signal:main:type|FR:BM}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:main:type|FR:PR}})}} (block system identification plate)
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:caption|}} (text displayed on the ''block system identification plate'')

=====Carré violet (mechanical)=====

The mechanical form consists of a purple square with a white border. To ensure visibility at night, it is fitted with a purple light positioned below the board.

<gallery>
File:CarreVM.svg|Mechanical Carré violet
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:main|FR:CV}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:form|sign}}

====Sémaphore====

A stop signal that can be passed under certain conditions. The signal may display either a steady or flashing red light. It is also equipped with an '''Identification Plate''' featuring one of the following inscriptions in white letters on a black background: 
* '''F''' (for ''Franchissable'', indicating a block of [https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Block_automatique_lumineux Block Automatique Lumineux])
* '''BM''' (indicating a block of [https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Block_manuel Block Manuel])
* '''PR''' (indicating a block of [https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Block_automatique_%C3%A0_permissivit%C3%A9_restreinte Block Automatique à Permissivité Restreinte])

<gallery>
File:Semaphore_F_BAL_F.svg|S aspect on an F-type signal head.
File:Semaphore_A_BAL_F.svg|S aspect on an A-type signal head.
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:main|FR:S}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:form|light}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:shape||({{TagValue|railway:signal:main:shape|FR:A}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:main:shape|FR:C}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:main:shape|FR:F}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:main:shape|FR:H}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:main:shape|FR:K}})}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:states|}} (→ [[FR:Key:railway:signal:main:states|available states]], separated by <code>;</code>)

Optional '''identification plate''':
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:type||({{TagValue|railway:signal:main:type|FR:F}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:main:type|FR:PR}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:main:type|FR:BM}})}}

=====Sémaphore (mechanical)=====

<gallery>
File:SemaphoreM.PNG|Mechanical semaphore signal.
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:main|FR:S}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:form|sign}}

====Guidon d'arrêt====

A stop signal that requires the driver to come to a complete stop before the signal. When in the open position, the signal does not display any specific indication other than the red band being extinguished. It is equipped with an identification plate with the inscription '''GA''' and may also have a marker plate, both featuring inscriptions in black letters on a white background.

<gallery>
File:Guidon_d'Arrêt.svg|Guidon d'Arrêt.
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:main|FR:GA}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:form|light}}

====Yellow band====

In some stations, the entrance [[#Carré|Carré signal]] may be equipped with a ''horizontal illuminated yellow band'' (French: '''Bande jaune lumineuse horizontale'''). This band is lit in addition to the [[Tag:railway:signal:main:states=FR:A|Caution]] ('''Avertissement''') light. It instructs the driver to be prepared to stop within a short distance, either due to the presence of vehicles or the closure of an intermediate stop signal. 

A [[#TVM_stop_marker|TVM stop marker]] may also be equipped with a yellow light band.

<gallery>
File:Bande_Jaune.svg|Yellow band.
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:short_route|FR:yellow_band}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:short_route:form|light}}

===Distant signals===

====Disque====

A '''Disque''' signal instructs the driver to proceed at sight ('''Marche à Vue''') as soon as possible or to stop before the first set of points (switch or crossing) protected by the signal. It is equipped with an identification plate bearing the inscription '''D''' in black letters on a white background.

<gallery>
File:Disque_BAPR_BM.svg|Luminous Disque signal.
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:distant|FR:D}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:distant:form|light}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:distant:states|}} (→ [[FR:Key:railway:signal:distant:states|available states]], separated by <code>;</code>)

=====Disque (mechanical)=====

<gallery>
File:DisqueMecanique.svg|Mechanical Disque signal.
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:distant|FR:D}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:distant:form|sign}}

====Avertissement====

An '''Avertissement''' (Caution) signal indicates the approach to a closed [[#Sémaphore|sémaphore]] of [https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Block_automatique_%C3%A0_permissivit%C3%A9_restreinte Block Automatique à Permissivité Restreinte] (BAPR). It is equipped with an identification plate bearing the inscription '''A''' in black letters on a white background.

<gallery>
File:Av_R_BAPR_BM.svg|Luminous Avertissement signal.
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:distant|FR:A}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:distant:form|light}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:distant:states|}} (→ [[FR:Key:railway:signal:distant:states|available states]], separated by <code>;</code>)

=====Avertissement (mechanical)=====

<gallery>
File:AvertissementMecanique.svg|Mechanical Avertissement signal.
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:distant|FR:A}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:distant:form|sign}}

===Disabled signal===

Signals not currently in use (e.g. deactivated or out of service) are marked with a white Saint Andrew's cross.

<gallery>
File:PermCancelled_H_BAL.svg|Disabled H-type signal head
</gallery>

Use one of the following tags depending on the signal type (main or distant):

* {{Tag|railway:signal:main:deactivated|yes}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:distant:deactivated|yes}}

===Light boxes===

Several illuminated [[#Shunting boards|shunting boards]] (D, G) and [[#Wrong-road signalling|wrong-road signalling boards]] (TECS, TSCS) may be installed in either a single light box (French: '''caisson lumineux''') or a double light box. These light boxes are usually installed alongside a [[#Carré|Carré]] signal. 

This is mapped using the <code>lightbox</code> property, which only applies when <code>form=light</code> is used; a mechanical board (<code>form=sign</code>) is always installed as a single board. See the individual board descriptions below for the applicable tags.

The <code>lightbox</code> property indicates the board's position within the light box:

* ''unset'' - single light box (default)
* <code>left</code> - the board occupies the left half of a double light box
* <code>right</code> - the board occupies the right half of a double light box

When two boards share a double light box, both are mapped '''on the same node'''. Each board is tagged separately, with one <code>lightbox</code> property set to <code>left</code> and the other to <code>right</code>. Both boards also share the same '''idreseau''' value (<code>*:ref</code>), which identifies the light box itself.

<gallery>
File:D TECS box.svg|Example of a double light box
</gallery>

For example, a light box displaying a '''D board''' on the left and a '''TECS board''' on the right would be tagged as follows:

* {{Tag|railway:signal:shunting_route|FR:destination}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:shunting_route:depot|FR:D}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:shunting_route:depot:form|light}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:shunting_route:depot:lightbox|left}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:shunting_route:depot:ref|123456}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:wrong_road|FR:transition}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:wrong_road:entry|FR:TECS}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:wrong_road:entry:form|light}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:wrong_road:entry:lightbox|right}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:wrong_road:entry:ref|123456}}

The combination of the <code>lightbox</code> property and the shared <code>*:ref</code> value indicates that both boards refer to the same physical light box. In this example, ''123456'' is a placeholder for an '''idreseau''' value.

===Instruction boards===
Instruction boards (French: '''Pancarte de consigne''') display operational instructions for train drivers. They are generally used in conjunction with another board or signal.

<gallery>
File:Pancarte Tirez au Pied du Signal.svg|'''Tirez au Pied du Signal''' instruction board
File:Pancarte Ne Franchir que sur Ordre du Poste 1+A.svg|'''Ne Franchir que sur Ordre du Poste 1+A''' instruction board
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:minor|FR:instruction_board}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:minor:form|sign}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:minor:caption|}} (text displayed on the board)

===Signal position indicators===
Signs that inform the driver about the side on which trackside signals are installed after a signalling or signal placement transition, such as a change between left-hand and right-hand running or between cab signalling and lineside signalling.

====Signals on right sign====
This sign indicates that trackside signals are installed on the right-hand side of the track.

<gallery>
File:Pancarte Signaux à Droite.svg|Signals on right sign
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:minor|FR:signals_on_right}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:minor:form|sign}}

====Signals on left sign====
This sign indicates that trackside signals are installed on the left-hand side of the track.

<gallery>
File:Pancarte Signaux à Gauche.svg|Signals on left sign
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:minor|FR:signals_on_left}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:minor:form|sign}}

===Mirlitons===
''Mirlitons'' are non-illuminated boards used to mark the approach to signals with reduced visibility. Three boards are generally installed approximately 100 m apart from each other and from the signal, displaying three, two and one diagonal black bands respectively. In some cases, fewer boards may be used. Smaller versions may be installed directly on the ground when required.

<gallery>
File:SNCF Mirliton I.svg|Mirliton I
File:SNCF Mirliton II.svg|Mirliton II
File:SNCF Mirliton III.svg|Mirliton III
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:distant|FR:mirliton}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:distant:type||({{TagValue|railway:signal:distant:type|I}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:distant:type|II}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:distant:type|III}})}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:distant:form|sign}}

===Permanent speed limits===

Permanent speed restrictions are signaled:
* either by [[#Ralentissement_30|Ralentissement 30]] (or 60) and [[#Rappel_30|Rappel 30]] (or 60) signals,
* or by ''speed limit indicators'' known as '''Tableaux Indicateurs de Vitesse limite''' ('''TIV'''). TIVs may be [[#Switchable_speed_indicators|switchable]], [[#Fixed_speed_indicators|fixed]] or [[#Pentagonal_speed_indicators|pentagonal]].

====Mechanical speed indicators====

=====Ralentissement 30=====

<gallery>
File:RalentissementM.svg|Mechanical slow 30 signal.
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit|FR:R30}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit:form|sign}}

=====Rappel 30=====

Rappel de ralentissement 30 (Reminder 30).

<gallery>
File:RappelRalentissementM.svg|Mechanical reminder 30 signal.
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit|FR:RR30}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit:form|sign}}

====Switchable speed indicators====

Points that can only be crossed at reduced speed in the thrown direction (approximately 60 km/h) are typically preceded by two ''switchable speed indicators'': a diamond-shaped '''TIV à Distance''' (TIV-D) followed by a ''speed limit reminder'' called '''TIV de Rappel''' (TIV-R).

These boards can be luminous or mechanical; when clear, they present a continuous white vertical band.

=====Switchable TIV-D=====

<gallery>
File:TIV_D_MOB_100.svg|Mechanical TIV-D ({{TagValue|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant:switchable:form|sign}})
File:TIV_Mobile_100.svg|Luminous TIV-D ({{TagValue|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant:switchable:form|light}})
File:TIV_Mobile_O.svg|Clear luminous TIV-D ({{TagValue|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant:switchable:form|light}})
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant|FR:speed_indicator}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant:switchable|FR:TIV-D}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant:switchable:form||
({{TagValue|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant:switchable:form|sign}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant:switchable:form|light}})}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant:switchable:speed|}} (speed as displayed on the signal, e.g. ''100'')
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant:switchable:turn_direction||({{TagValue|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant:switchable:turn_direction|left}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant:switchable:turn_direction|through}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant:switchable:turn_direction|right}})}} (route to which the speed restriction applies)

=====Switchable TIV-R=====

The '''TIV-R''' is always paired with the [[#Carré|Carré]] signal preceding the point.

<gallery>
File:TIV_R_MOB_60.svg|Mechanical TIV-R ({{TagValue|railway:signal:speed_limit:switchable:form|sign}})
File:TIV_Rappel_Lumineux_60.svg|Luminous TIV-R ({{TagValue|railway:signal:speed_limit:switchable:form|light}})
TIV_Rappel_Lumineux_O.svg|Clear luminous TIV-R ({{TagValue|railway:signal:speed_limit:switchable:form|light}})
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit|FR:speed_indicator}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit:switchable|FR:TIV-R}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit:switchable:form||
({{TagValue|railway:signal:speed_limit:switchable:form|sign}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:speed_limit:switchable:form|light}})}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit:switchable:speed|}} (speed as displayed on the signal, e.g. 60)
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit:switchable:turn_direction||({{TagValue|railway:signal:speed_limit:switchable:turn_direction|left}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:speed_limit:switchable:turn_direction|through}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:speed_limit:switchable:turn_direction|right}})}} (route to which the speed restriction applies)

====Chevron pointe en bas====

If necessary, the location of the point (or the first point in the case of successive points) is identified by a downward-pointing chevron.

In some cases, particularly at diverging exits from certain station tracks, a 30 km/h speed reminder may apply to a trailing point rather than to a facing point. In such cases, the location of the relevant point may instead be identified by an [[#Chevron_pointe_en_haut|upward-pointing chevron]] ('''Chevron pointe en haut''').

<gallery>
File:Chevron_bas.svg|Chevron pointe en bas
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:minor|FR:chevron}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:minor:form|sign}}

====Fixed speed indicators====

=====Fixed Ordinary-type TIV-D=====

Fixed distant speed indicators of the ordinary type (French: '''TIV fixes à distance du type ordinaire''') are square-shaped when indicating a speed reduction of less than 40 km/h, and diamond-shaped otherwise. Diamond-shaped indicators are equipped with a crocodile.

<gallery>
File:TIV_Distance_80.svg|Square TIV-D
TIV_Distance_Crocodile_40.svg|Diamond-shaped TIV-D
</gallery>

Common tags:

* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant|FR:speed_indicator}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant:fixed|FR:TIV-D}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant:fixed:form|sign}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant:fixed:speed|}} (speed as displayed on the signal, e.g. 80)

Additional tag for diamond-shaped indicators only:

* {{Tag|railway:crocodile|yes}}

=====Z sign=====
The '''Z''' sign is the execution signal indicating the start of the section to be traveled at limited speed.

<gallery>
File:Tableau_Z.svg|Z sign
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit|FR:marker}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit:main|FR:Z}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit:main:form|sign}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit:main:function|entry}}

=====R sign=====
The '''R''' sign indicates the end of the section where the speed limit is required and the return to normal speed ('''Reprise de vitesse''').

<gallery>
File:Tableau_R.svg|R sign
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit|FR:marker}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit:main|FR:R}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit:main:form|sign}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit:main:function|exit}}

=====Fixed B-type TIV-D=====

B-type fixed distant speed indicators ('''TIV fixes à distance du type B''') apply to trains authorized to exceed 140 km/h. When only a B-type indicator is present, the indicated speed limit also applies to EMUs and DMUs.

<gallery>
File:FR-TIV-type-B-160.svg|Fixed B-type TIV-D
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant|FR:speed_indicator}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant:fast|FR:TIV-D}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant:fast:form|sign}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant:fast:speed|}}

=====Fixed C-type TIV-D=====

C-type fixed distant speed indicators ('''TIV fixes à distance du type C''') specifically apply to ''railcars'', ''EMUs'', and ''DMUs''.

<gallery>
File:FR_TIV-type-C-180.svg|Fixed C-type TIV-D
</gallery>

When a B-type and a C-type fixed distant speed indicator are paired, the speed limit shown by the B-type indicator applies only to trains authorized to exceed 140 km/h. The C-type indicator serves as a reminder of the upstream speed limit for railcars, EMUs, and DMUs.

If the speed limit differs between pendular and non-pendular EMUs and DMUs, the C-type indicator displays two numbers. The lower section, in italics and showing the higher value, indicates the limit for pendular trains; the upper section shows the limit for non-pendular EMUs and DMUs.

* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant|FR:speed_indicator}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant:railcar|FR:TIV-D}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant:railcar:form|sign}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:speed_limit_distant:railcar:speed|}} (separated by <code>;</code> if more than one speed limit has to be specified)

====Speed limit announcement (P board)====

The P board announces a distant speed indicator (TIV-D) for lines equipped with pre-announcement signalling. This board applies only to trains running at speeds higher than 160 km/h and requires the train to pass the next TIV-D at a speed lower than 160 km/h. This sign is lit at night.

</gallery>

Pentagonal TIVs typically concern freight trains and possibly certain locomotive series. The TIV figure specifies the maximum speed in tens of kilometers per hour (e.g. 5 stands for 50 km/h).

These boards are used on double-track sections equipped with wrong-road signalling installations, also known in French as '''Installations Permanentes de ContreSens''' (IPCS).

===Cab signalling===

To allow trains to run safely at speeds above 220 km/h, traditional lineside signals are replaced by in-cab signalling systems. These systems transmit movement authorities and speed instructions directly to the driver's cab.

In France, the two main cab signalling systems are [https://wikipedia.org/wiki/Transmission_Voie-Machine Transmission Voie-Machine (TVM)] and the [https://wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Train_Control_System European Train Control System (ETCS)].

=====CAB boards=====
The train is directed towards a cab signalling line. One or more boards of this type precede the entry.

<gallery>
File:Signalisation_de_Cabine_Distant.svg|Cab signalling line advance board
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:train_protection_distant|FR:CAB}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:train_protection_distant:form|sign}}


The train enters a cab signalling line. This board is at the position of the last signal or immediately downstream of that signal.

<gallery>
File:Signalisation_de_Cabine.svg|Cab signalling line entry board
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:train_protection|FR:CAB}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:train_protection:form|sign}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:train_protection:function|entry}}


The train is returning to a traditional lateral signalling line.

<gallery>
File:Fin_de_Signalisation_de_Cabine.svg|Cab signalling line exit board
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:train_protection|FR:/CAB}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:train_protection:form|sign}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:train_protection:function|exit}}

'''Note:''' prepend <code>/</code> to the type to specify the crossed-out variant of a sign/board identified by its displayed name or acronym (''function=exit'').

=====Cancellation signal (RATP)=====
The [https://wikipedia.org/wiki/Syst%C3%A8me_d%27aide_%C3%A0_la_conduite,%C3%A0_l%27exploitation_et%C3%A0_la_maintenance SACEM] (French: '''Système d'Aide à la Conduite, à l'Exploitation et à la Maintenance''') is a cab signalling system used on the [https://wikipedia.org/wiki/RER_A RER A] line in the Paris region. When SACEM is active, most lineside signal indications are cancelled and replaced by an illuminated Saint-Andrew's cross (X), with the exception of stop signals, the clearing light (''œilleton''), route indicators and partially occupied track indicators.

===Electrified railway lines===

====Neutral sections====

A neutral section (French: ''zone de sectionnement'') is a grounded catenary section, isolated on both sides, used to separate portions of track either powered by different substations or phases, or when switching voltages from 1500 V DC to 25 kV AC and vice versa, or to accommodate different voltages and frequencies in cross-border areas.

=====Power-off advance signal=====

The advance signal indicates the presence of a neutral section ahead, located at the specified distance (in meters).

<gallery caption="Various arrangements of the signal">
File:Pancarte à distance Sectionnement à 500 m.svg|Mechanical signal ({{TagValue|railway:signal:electricity:form|sign}})
File:Caisson à distance Sectionnement à 500 m.svg|Light box ({{TagValue|railway:signal:electricity:form|light}})
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:electricity|FR:power_off_advance}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:electricity:type|power_off_advance}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:electricity:form||({{TagValue|railway:signal:electricity:form|sign}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:electricity:form|light}})}}

Optional tags:
* {{Tag|railway:signal:electricity:distance|}} (distance shown on the sign, in meters)

=====Power-off signal=====

The power-off (French: ''Coupez courant'') signal requires the main circuit breaker to be opened when passing through a neutral section, which it traverses using its own kinetic energy (''marche sur l'erre'').

File:Couper_Courant.svg|Mechanical signal ({{TagValue|railway:signal:electricity:form|sign}})

</gallery>

====Pantograph down====

=====Pantograph down advance signal=====

The pantograph down (French: ''Baissez panto'') advance signal instructs the lowering of the train's pantograph(s) under specific circumstances:

* '''Transition from 1500 V DC to 25 kV AC''': Required when switching from direct current (DC) to alternating current (AC) power supply.
* '''Between Two 25 kV Substations''': Necessary due to phase shift, potentially creating voltage differences of up to 70 kV in case of opposite phases.
* '''Phase Change''': Used to redistribute the electrical load within the network.
* '''Cross-border Areas''': Needed when crossing borders where different electrical systems may be in operation.
* '''Crossing Certain Structures''': Specific structures may require the pantograph to be lowered for safety or operational reasons.

<gallery caption="Various arrangements of the signal">
File:Signal à distance Baissez Panto.svg|Mechanical signal ({{TagValue|railway:signal:electricity:form|sign}})

File:Caisson à distance Baissez Panto (wide).svg|Wide light box ({{TagValue|railway:signal:electricity:form|light}} + {{TagValue|railway:signal:electricity:lightbox|wide}})
</gallery>

({{TagValue|railway:signal:electricity:form|sign}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:electricity:form|light}})}}

=====Pantograph up signal=====

This signal marks the end of the catenary section requiring pantographs to be lowered. Pantographs may be raised after passing the signal.

The signal may also indicate the catenary voltage and installation type. The presence of an installation type indicates a constant contact wire height and requires the pantograph stop to be set. When no installation type is indicated, the contact wire height is variable and the pantograph stop must be removed.

Boards marking the entry and exit of a switchable station, an electrical frontier where
the catenary voltage can be switched. Light boxes inside indicate the current voltage.

====End of catenary====
Beyond this sign, the line is no longer electrified and only diesel or dual-mode trains can continue.

</gallery>

====Frost board====

'''GIVRE''' (frost) boards are installed on some 1500 V DC electrified lines. When a driver encounters such an illuminated board, the second pantograph must be raised to improve current collection: the first pantograph clears ice from the catenary, improving contact for the second one.

The second pantograph is lowered when another frost board in the off state is encountered, after verbal authorization, or when no icing conditions are observed.

<gallery>
File:Tableau_GIVRE.svg|Mechanical board ({{TagValue|railway:signal:electricity:form|sign}})
File:Tableau_GIVRE_box.svg|Light box ({{TagValue|railway:signal:electricity:form|light}})
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:electricity|FR:frost}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:electricity:form||({{TagValue|railway:signal:electricity:form|sign}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:electricity:form|light}})}}

====Bimode operation====
This distant sign announces the approach of a non-electrified section for bi-mode trains only. It accompanies the [[#Pantograph down advance signal|distant]] and [[#Pantograph down signal|execution]] pantograph down signals when these signals apply exclusively to bi-mode trains. In this case, they are not followed by a [[#Pantograph up signal|pantograph up signal]].

<gallery>
File:Pancarte_BIMODE_A.svg|Bi-mode operation entry board
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:bimode|FR:BIMODE}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:bimode:form|sign}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:bimode:function|entry}}

Optional tags:

This distant sign announces the exit from a non-electrified section for bi-mode trains only. This sign accompanies the [[#Pantograph up signal|pantograph up signal]] when the signal applies exclusively to bi-mode trains. It is not preceded by the [[#Pantograph down advance signal|distant]] and [[#Pantograph execution|execution]] pantograph down signals.

</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:bimode:function|exit}}

===Stops===
Stop signs require the driver to bring the train to a complete stop before the sign. The exact procedure for resuming movement depends on the sign type ([[#Arrêt signs|Arrêt]], [[#Stop signs|Stop]] or [[#StopMarker|marker]]).

====Arrêt signs====
The driver must stop before the sign and wait for a verbal order before passing, if passing is required.

===Passenger stops===

Passenger stop signs apply to a category of train. The categories are nested, from the most general to the most specific, and a sign is tagged with the '''most specific''' category that applies to it:

* [[#Passenger stops for any trains|any]] – any train, whatever its category (e.g. the length signs);
** [[#Passenger stops for conventional trains|conventional]] – all trains except high-speed: locomotive-hauled trains, EMUs, and DMUs;
*** [[#Passenger stops for regional trains|regional]] – regional EMUs (Z 57000 / ''Régio 2N'');
*** [[#Passenger stops for suburban trains (RER)|suburban]] – suburban EMUs (Z 50000 / ''Francilien'') and the RER length signs ;
** [[#Passenger stops for high-speed trains|highspeed]] – high-speed trains (TGV).

====Passenger stops for any trains====

=====L... sign=====
Stopping point for a train of the specified length, regardless of its type.

File:Pancarte L110.svg|L110 - 110-metre train

File:Pancarte L200RBT.svg|L200RBT - 200-metre train (in track, for reversing)
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:stop|FR:passenger_stop}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:stop:any|FR:train_length}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:stop:any:form|sign}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:stop:any:length|}} (train length in metres, e.g. ''110'' or ''220'')

Optional tags:
* {{Tag|railway:signal:stop:any:reversal|yes}} (L ''length'' RBT)

====Stations====

====Train departure====

=====Reporting Plate=====

In general, the driver of a train stopped by a [[#Carré|Carré]], a [[#Carré_violet|Carré violet]], or a [[#Guidon_d'arrêt|Guidon d'arrêt]] must report to the signaller if the signal does not clear immediately.

If a signal is equipped with a telephone that is not located in its immediate vicinity, its location may be indicated by a reporting plate ('''Plaque de Reconnaissance''' in French).

<gallery caption="Various arrangements of the plate">
File:Plaque de reconnaissance avec VAT.svg|Reporting plate
File:Plaque de reconnaissance différée avec VAT.svg|Delayed reporting plate ({{TagValue|railway:signal:departure:type|delayed}})
File:Plaque de dispense de reconnaissance avec VAT.svg|Reporting exemption plate ({{TagValue|railway:signal:departure:type|exempt}})
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:departure|FR:reporting}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:departure:form|sign}}

Optional tags:

- Alternative types:
* {{Tag|railway:signal:departure:type||({{TagValue|railway:signal:departure:type|delayed}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:departure:type|exempt}})}}

- If an arrow indicates the direction to the telephone:
* {{Tag|railway:signal:departure:phone:direction||({{TagValue|railway:signal:departure:phone:direction|left}}/{{TagValue|railway:signal:departure:phone:direction|right}})}}

- If the plate is equipped with a telephone call indicator (French: '''Voyant d'Appel Téléphonique''', also known as '''VAT'''):
* {{Tag|railway:signal:departure:phone:indicator|yes}}

Note: Telephone call indicators (VAT) are no longer installed on lines equipped with [[#Network marker|GSM-R]].

=====Departure request=====

Some [[#Carré|Carré]] signals are equipped with a '''Demande de Départ''' (DD) plate. The driver waiting for departure must, one minute before the scheduled departure time or if they notice the corresponding Carré signal has opened, request departure authorization by telephone.

<gallery>
File:Plaque_DD.svg|'''Demande de Départ''' (DD) plate
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:departure|FR:DD}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:departure:form|sign}}

=====Departure authorization=====

On certain tracks, authorization for departure may be given to the driver by a flashing half-white, half-green '''Signal Lumineux de Départ''' (SLD), also known as a '''Signal Lumineux d'Autorisation de Mouvement'''.

<gallery>
File:SLD_box.gif|Signal Lumineux d'Autorisation de Mouvement
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:departure|FR:SLD}} 
* {{Tag|railway:signal:departure:form|light}}


Alternatively, departure authorization may be given simply by the opening of the corresponding [[#Carré|Carré]] signal; these Carré signals are identified by a half-white, half-green plate.

<gallery>
File:Plaque_mi-blanche_mi-verte.svg|half-white, half-green plate
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:departure|FR:departure_marker}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:departure:form|sign}}


=====Dispositifs d'Aide à la Mise en Mouvement=====
Dispositifs d'Aide à la Mise en Mouvement (DAMM) are installed at stations where the exit signal is not directly visible to the driver from the train's normal departure point, for example because of a curved platform or other obstructions. The DAMM allows the driver to know when they may begin moving towards the exit signal in order to observe its aspect and receive the movement authority provided by the signal.

A DAMM is illuminated when the driver is authorized to begin moving and is unlit otherwise.

<gallery>
File:DAMM allumé.svg|Illuminated DAMM
File:DAMM éteint.svg|Unlit DAMM
</gallery>

===Converging tracks===

====Chevron pointe en haut====

Upward-pointing chevrons indicate either an exit from a junction of converging tracks or, in some stations, the point beyond which trains must not proceed when a stop is required.

<gallery>
File:Chevron_haut.svg|Chevron pointe en haut ({{TagValue|railway:signal:minor:type|up}})
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:minor|FR:chevron}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:minor:type|up}} (''down'' by default)
* {{Tag|railway:signal:minor:form|sign}}

====Tableau Lumineux de Correspondance====

A '''Tableau Lumineux de Correspondance''' (TLC) for converging tracks is a signal installed to the left of the track it addresses and is normally off. At any given time, it can display one of the following:

- A white letter '''T''', either ''fixed'' if the group signal is open or ''flashing'', if the group signal is closed.

- The [[#Signal Lumineux de Départ|Signal Lumineux de Départ]] if applicable.

- A red and white checkerboard, which has the same meaning as the [[#StopMarker|Jalon d'Arrêt]] and is used instead of the [[#Chevron_pointe_en_haut|chevron]].

<gallery>
File:TLC-T.svg|The group signal is clear
File:TLC-T.gif|The group signal is at danger
File:TLC-SLD.gif|Signal Lumineux de Départ
File:TLC-C.svg|Stop marker
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:minor|FR:TLC}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:minor:form|light}}

====Tableau Indicateur de Provenance====

At the exit of some service track yards, a '''Tableau Indicateur de Provenance''' (TIP), a track indicator, complements the [[#Chevron_pointe_en_haut|chevron]]. It can display any of the numbers designating each of the tracks. When the TIP displays a number, the driver on the corresponding track is allowed to cross the chevron. When the group signal is closed, the driver can advance to an agreed point, usually in preparation for a reversing movement.

<gallery>
File:TIP_box.svg|Tableau Indicateur de Provenance
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:minor|FR:TIP}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:minor:form|light}}

===Service tracks and shunting===

====Signal Lumineux de Manœuvre====

A '''Signal Lumineux de Manœuvre''' (SLM) is installed in some installations to facilitate shunting operations on main tracks (for example, pushing a train into a siding) or on service tracks. It consists of three white lights, which are normally unlit.

The SLM can display the following aspects:
* '''Pull''' (''Tirez''): two white lights alternating on a vertical line.
* '''Push back''' (''Refoulez''): two white lights alternating on a horizontal line.
* '''Stop''' (''Arrêtez''): all lights extinguished.
* '''Observe hand shunting signals''' (''Observez les signaux à main de manœuvre''): all three white lights lit simultaneously and steadily.

Several similar signals may be installed along the same track to mark the full extent of the shunting area. In such cases, they are numbered with Roman numerals in descending order (e.g. III, II, I), with SLM I being the closest to the switch and identifying the terminal signal of the shunting area.

Note: '''SLM''' are no longer installed on new installations due to the widespread availability of shunting radio, either permanently installed on shunting vehicles or provided as portable equipment on line locomotives.

<gallery>
File:SLM_pull.gif|'''Pull''' aspect
File:SLM_push.gif|'''Push back''' aspect
File:SLM stop.svg|'''Stop''' aspect
File:SLM all.svg|'''Observe hand shunting signals''' aspect
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:shunting|FR:SLM}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:shunting:form|light}}
* {{Tag|ref||(I/II/III/IV/V)}} (marker plate with Roman numerals)

====Shunting boards====
The [[#D board|D]], [[#G board|G]], [[#Imp board|Imp]] and [[#Distant buffer stop board|Distant buffer stop]] boards are normally grouped with the preceding [[#Carré|Carré]] signal before the facing point of the switch when they are ''switchable''. When ''fixed'', they are usually installed beyond the switch.

Buffer stops are normally identified by a purple or red light. As a temporary measure, they may instead be identified by the [[#Buffer stop board (H board)|H board]].

===Level crossings===

Most French level crossings are equipped with Automatic Light Signalling (SAL) (French: Signalisation Automatique Lumineuse et sonore), which warns road users using flashing red lights, audible alarms and, where fitted, barriers. 

Depending on the installation, the warning sequence may be initiated automatically, manually by the train crew, or by a radio command transmitted by the train driver.

====Level crossing announcement====

This announcement sign informs the driver that they are approaching an unguarded level crossing where specific operating instructions apply.

<gallery>
File:Pancarte PN d'Annonce.svg|Level crossing advance sign
File:Pancarte PN d'Annonce avec Pancarte Radio.svg|Level crossing advance sign with ''Radio'' sign
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:crossing_hint|FR:PN}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:crossing_hint:form|sign}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:crossing_hint:number|}} (level crossing number e.g. ''46'')
* {{Tag|railway:signal:crossing_hint:distance|}} (distance in meters e.g. ''300'')

When fitted with an additional ''Radio'' sign, it indicates that the approaching level crossing is operated by radio control. In this case, the following tag must also be specified:
* {{Tag|railway:signal:crossing_hint:type|radio_controlled}}

'''Note:''' The ''Radio'' sign is not used where all level crossings on the line or track are radio-controlled.

====Radio-controlled level crossing====

This board, installed approximately 350 m before the level crossing, marks the location where the train driver must transmit a radio command that initiates the warning sequence.

<gallery>
File:Pancarte Cde Radio.svg|Radio command sign
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:crossing_hint|FR:radio_command}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:crossing_hint:form|sign}}

====Level crossing ahead====

This sign is placed immediately before the level crossing and identifies the crossing by its number. It also indicates how the crossing is operated.

* '''Automatic mode''' (no white band): the warning sequence is initiated automatically by the approaching train.

* '''Manual mode''' (white band): the warning sequence must be initiated by the train crew according to operating instructions.

<gallery>
File:Pancarte PN de Proximité.svg|Automatic level crossing sign
File:Pancarte PN avec Bandeau Blanc.svg|Manually operated level crossing sign ({{TagValue|railway:signal:crossing_info:automatic|no}})
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:crossing_info|FR:PN}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:crossing_info:form|sign}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:crossing_info:number|}} (level crossing number as shown on the sign, e.g. ''44'' or ''116'')

If the level crossing is manually operated, the following tag must be specified:
* {{Tag|railway:signal:crossing_info:automatic|no}} (''yes'' by default)

====Signal de Franchissement Conditionnel====
Radio-controlled level crossings are additionally equipped with a '''Signal de Franchissement Conditionnel''' (SFC). This signal consists of one or two ''green lights'', arranged vertically or horizontally, and installed close to or above the level crossing sign.

When illuminated, the SFC confirms that the level crossing has been activated successfully and is securely closed, authorizing the train to proceed without stopping at the ''PN'' sign. When unlit, it is equivalent to a stop indication.

<gallery>
File:Feux Verts.svg|Vertically arranged green lights
File:Feux Verts Horizontaux.svg|Horizontally arranged green lights
</gallery>

* {{Tag|railway:signal:crossing|FR:SFC}}
* {{Tag|railway:signal:crossing:form|light}}

Optional tags:
* {{Tag|railway:signal:crossing:arrangement|vertical}} (horizontal by default)

The '''S''' sign indicates locations where the driver must sound the horn, such as when approaching unguarded level crossings, entering tunnels, or passing through areas with reduced visibility.

When a '''J''' plate is present below the '''S''' sign, it indicates that the whistling obligation applies only during ''daytime'' (between 07:00 and 20:00).

===Snowplow===
The '''snowplow lowering signal''' (type '''down''') indicates where trains equipped with a snowplow must lower the equipment. The '''snowplow raising signal''' (type '''up''') indicates where the equipment must be raised to avoid striking obstructions.

===Border signals===
Near the French–Swiss border, some railway signals belonging to the Swiss signalling system can be found on French territory while carrying SNCF Réseau identifiers. This section describes the main Swiss signals encountered in these border areas.

For more information about Swiss railway signalling, please see [[DE:OpenRailwayMap/Tagging_in_Switzerland|Tagging in Switzerland]].
